summary: This bill gives Executive Order 14319 the force and effect of law to prevent woke AI in the Federal Government.

scores.thoughts: The bill consists of a single section codifying an executive order on AI usage in the federal government. It contains no provisions, authorizations, or directives related to federal expenditures, appropriations, or budget authority.
The bill text makes no reference to tax policy, rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
No provisions in the bill address healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market structures.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
Nothing in the bill pertains to immigration policy, border security, visas, or related protections.
The bill does not engage with reproductive health policy or abortion access in any manner.
No elements of the bill address defense spending, military procurement, or national security budgets.
The legislation contains no environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions related to climate or natural resources.
The bill does not modify, expand, or restrict any welfare, nutrition, housing, or income-support programs.
No provisions relate to schools, federal education funding, curriculum, or school choice.
The bill is silent on controlled substances, enforcement priorities, or decriminalization.
Nothing in the text concerns sentencing, policing, incarceration, or justice-system reforms.
The bill does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
No fiscal measures, deficit targets, or debt-ceiling provisions appear in the legislation.

While the underlying executive order concerns ideological content in federal AI systems (which can intersect with cultural issues), the bill itself is a narrow codification measure and does not directly alter legal protections or rights for any group.
The legislation contains no foreign-assistance authorizations or funding directives.
No provisions relate to voting procedures, election administration, or voter qualifications.
Although the bill concerns federal use of AI, it does not establish privacy standards, data-protection rules, or regulatory oversight mechanisms for technology companies.
The bill does not address collective bargaining, worker protections, or union governance.
The bill text does not create, modify, or balance religious exemptions against anti-discrimination requirements.
